     2	
     3	## Description
     4	
     5	Update the framework's testing documentation to describe the new `composer seed-tests` command, the seeding requirement, and the shutdown handler behavior.
     6	
     7	## Scope

    10

    19	2. The documentation explains that running tests requires a pre-seeded test database and that missing system users will produce a `BootException` directing the developer to run `composer seed-tests`.
    20	3. The documentation mentions that `TestSuiteBootstrap` registers a shutdown handler to roll back orphaned transactions, preventing InnoDB lock wait timeouts from crashed test processes.

1	# Testing
     2	
     3	Comprehensive guide to the Application Framework's test infrastructure, conventions, and execution.
     4	
     5	---
     6	
     7	## Overview
     8	
     9	| Aspect | Detail |
    10	|---|---|
    11	| **Framework** | PHPUnit >= 13.0 |
    12	| **PHP version** | 8.4+ |
    13	| **Config file** | `phpunit.xml` (project root) |
    14	| **Bootstrap** | `tests/bootstrap.php` |
    15	| **Test count** | ~155 unit test files + 2 integration test files |
    16	| **Test suite** | Single suite: `Framework Tests` (all tests under `tests/AppFrameworkTests/`) |
    17	
    18	---
    19	
    20	## Directory Structure
    21	
    22	```
    23	tests/
    24	├── bootstrap.php                    # PHPUnit bootstrap — boots the framework test application
    25	├── AppFrameworkTests/               # All unit test files (one folder per module)

    69	│   ├── LDAP/
    70	│   └── Logging/
    71	├── AppFrameworkTestClasses/         # Base test cases, traits, mocks, stubs
    72	│   ├── API/                         # API test cases and stubs
    73	│   ├── Collection/
    74	│   ├── Stubs/                       # Stub implementations for testing
    75	│   ├── Traits/                      # Shared test traits (paired with interfaces)
    76	│   ├── ApplicationTestCase.php      # Primary base test case (extends PHPUnit TestCase)
    77	│   ├── ApplicationTestCaseInterface.php
    78	│   └── ...                          # Domain-specific base test cases
    79	├── application/                     # Framework Test Application (working implementation)
    80	│   └── assets/classes/              # Test application classes
    81	├── assets/                          # Test fixtures

    84	└── sql/                             # Source SQL files for the test database
    85	```
    86	
    87	---
    88	
    89	## Test File Naming Convention
    90	
    91	All unit test files under `tests/AppFrameworkTests/` must follow this convention:
    92	
    93	| Element | Requirement | Example |
    94	|---|---|---|
    95	| **File name** | Must match the class name exactly (`.php` extension) | `CoreTest.php` |
    96	| **Class name** | Must end in `Test`, PascalCase | `CoreTest` |
    97	| **Namespace** | Must match the directory path under `AppFrameworkTests\` | `AppFrameworkTests\Disposables` |
    98	| **Declaration** | Must include `declare(strict_types=1);` | — |
    99	
   100	### Correct structure

101	
   102	```php
   103	<?php
   104	
   105	declare(strict_types=1);
   106	
   107	namespace AppFrameworkTests\Disposables;
   108	
   109	use AppFrameworkTestClasses\ApplicationTestCase;
   110	
   111	class CoreTest extends ApplicationTestCase
   112	{
   113	    // ...
   114	}
   115	```
   116	
   117	PHPUnit discovers tests by scanning the `tests/AppFrameworkTests/` directory tree for `.php` files. If the **class name does not match the file name**, PHPUnit emits a "Class X cannot be found" warning and the test is silently skipped. Always verify that both match before committing a new test file.
   118	
   119	> **Note on `AppFrameworkTests\Global`:** `Global` is a reserved word in PHP. Tests that previously lived under the `Global/` directory have been placed in `AppFrameworkTests\GlobalTests` instead to avoid parser errors.
   120	
   121	---
   122	
   123	## Running Tests
   124	
   125	### Composer Scripts
   126	
   127	All test execution goes through Composer scripts defined in `composer.json`:
   128	
   129	| Command | Purpose | Example |
   130	|---|---|---|
   131	| `composer test-file -- <path>` | Run a single test file | `composer test-file -- tests/AppFrameworkTests/DBHelper/CollectionTest.php` |
   132	| `composer test-filter -- <pattern>` | Run tests matching a name filter | `composer test-filter -- CollectionTest::testSomeMethod` |
   133	| `composer test-suite -- <name>` | Run all tests in a named suite | `composer test-suite -- "Framework Tests"` |
   134	| `composer test-group -- <group>` | Run tests in a PHPUnit group | `composer test-group -- SomeGroup` |
   135	
   136	All scripts pass `--no-progress` to PHPUnit by default (except `composer test`).
   137	
   138	### Choosing the Right Scope
   139	
   140	1. **Changed a single class?** → `composer test-file` with its test file.
   141	2. **Changed a module?** → `composer test-filter -- ModuleName` to match by class name.
   142	3. **Unsure which tests cover a change?** → `composer test-filter -- ClassName`.
   143	4. **Full suite** → `composer test` (runs all tests).
   144	
   145	---
   146	
   147	## Base Test Cases
   148	
   149	All tests extend `ApplicationTestCase`, which extends PHPUnit's `TestCase`. Specialized base classes provide domain-specific setup:
   150	
   151	| Base Class | Namespace | Purpose |
   152	|---|---|---|
   153	| `ApplicationTestCase` | `AppFrameworkTestClasses` | Primary base — boots the application, provides common helpers, transaction management |
   154	| `AjaxTestCase` | `AppFrameworkTestClasses` | AJAX method testing |
   155	| `APITestCase` | `AppFrameworkTestClasses\API` | API method testing |
   156	| `APIClientTestCase` | `AppFrameworkTestClasses\API` | API client testing |
   157	| `CountriesTestCase` | `AppFrameworkTestClasses` | Country collection tests |
   158	| `DBHelperTestCase` | `AppFrameworkTestClasses` | Database helper tests |
   159	| `FormTestCase` | `AppFrameworkTestClasses` | Form building/validation tests |
   160	| `LDAPTestCase` | `AppFrameworkTestClasses` | LDAP connectivity tests |
   161	| `MediaTestCase` | `AppFrameworkTestClasses` | Media library tests |
   162	| `NewsTestCase` | `AppFrameworkTestClasses` | News central tests |
   163	| `RequestLogTestCase` | `AppFrameworkTestClasses` | Request logging tests |
   164	| `RevisionableTestCase` | `AppFrameworkTestClasses` | Revisionable record tests |
   165	| `TaggingTestCase` | `AppFrameworkTestClasses` | Tagging system tests |
   166	| `UserTestCase` | `AppFrameworkTestClasses` | User management tests |
   167	
   168	---
   169	
   170	## Shared Test Traits
   171	
   172	Reusable test behavior is implemented via trait + interface pairs in `tests/AppFrameworkTestClasses/Traits/`. A test class implements the interface and uses the trait:
   173	
   174	| Trait | Interface | Purpose |
   175	|---|---|---|
   176	| `ConnectorTestTrait` | `ConnectorTestInterface` | Connector testing |
   177	| `DBHelperTestTrait` | `DBHelperTestInterface` | DBHelper testing |
   178	| `DataGridTestTrait` | — | DataGrid testing |
   179	| `ImageMediaTestTrait` | `ImageMediaTestInterface` | Image media testing |
   180	| `MythologyTestTrait` | `MythologyTestInterface` | Test application mythology testing |
   181	| `OperationResultTestTrait` | `OperationResultTestInterface` | Operation result testing |
   182	| `RevisionableTestTrait` | — | Revisionable record testing |
   183	
   184	API-specific traits in `tests/AppFrameworkTestClasses/API/`:
   185	
   186	| Trait | Interface | Purpose |
   187	|---|---|---|
   188	| `APIClientTestTrait` | `APIClientTestInterface` | API client testing |
   189	| `APIMethodTestTrait` | `APIMethodTestInterface` | API method testing |
   190	
   191	---
   192	
   193	## Bootstrap Process
   194	
   195	The test bootstrap (`tests/bootstrap.php`):
   196	
   197	1. Defines `APP_ROOT` pointing to `tests/application/` (the framework test application).
   198	2. Defines `TESTS_ROOT`, `APP_INSTALL_FOLDER`, `APP_VENDOR_PATH` constants.
   199	3. Sets `APP_FRAMEWORK_TESTS = true` to signal the framework's own test suite.
   200	4. Requires the framework bootstrap (`src/classes/Application/Bootstrap/Bootstrap.php`).
   201	5. Initializes `Application_Bootstrap` and boots the `TestSuiteBootstrap` class.
   202	
   203	This means the full application stack is available in tests (database, services, configuration).
   204	
   205	---
   206	
   207	## Framework Test Application
   208	
   209	The framework includes a working test application in `tests/application/` that provides concrete implementations of framework abstractions. This application is used by the test suite to exercise framework features against real database tables and screens.
   210	
   211	---
   212	
   213	## Local Test Environment Setup
   214	
   215	The test suite requires local configuration files that are **not committed** to the repository. Before running tests for the first time, copy the distribution templates and configure them for the local environment:
   216	
   217	1. Copy `tests/application/config/test-db-config.dist.php` → `tests/application/config/test-db-config.php`
   218	2. Copy `tests/application/config/test-ui-config.dist.php` → `tests/application/config/test-ui-config.php`
   219	3. Copy `tests/application/config/test-cas-config.dist.php` → `tests/application/config/test-cas-config.php`
   220	
   221	Edit `test-db-config.php` and set the correct database host, name, user, and password. The database name defaults to `app_framework_testsuite`; import `tests/sql/testsuite.sql` to initialise it.
   222	
   223	Edit `test-ui-config.php` and adjust `TESTS_BASE_URL` to the URL at which `tests/application` is reachable on the local webserver.
   224	
   225	`test-cas-config.php` is only required when `TESTS_SESSION_TYPE` is set to `CAS` in `test-ui-config.php`. For most local runs the default `NoAuth` session type is sufficient and the CAS config can be left as-is.
   226	
   227	---
   228	
   229	## Stubs
   230	
   231	Located in `tests/AppFrameworkTestClasses/Stubs/`:
   232	
   233	| Stub | Purpose |
   234	|---|---|
   235	| `ClientFormStub` | Client form stub |
   236	| `HiddenVariablesStub` | Hidden variables stub |
   237	| `IDTableCollectionStub` | ID table collection stub |
   238	| `LegacyUIRenderableStub` | Legacy UI renderable stub |
   239	| `PropertizableStub` | Propertizable stub |
   240	| `StringableStub` | Stringable stub |
   241	| `ValidatableStub` | Validatable stub |
   242	
   243	Additional stubs exist in subdirectories: `Stubs/Admin/`, `Stubs/DBHelper/`, `Stubs/Revisionables/`, `Stubs/Session/`, `Stubs/UI/`.
   244	
   245	---
   246	
   247	## API Test Stub Placement
   248	
   249	API method stubs that invoke `processReturn()` must be placed in the test application's source directory:
   250	
   251	```
   252	tests/application/assets/classes/TestDriver/API/
   253	```
   254	
   255	**Do not** place such stubs in `tests/AppFrameworkTestClasses/` — they will not be discovered by the method index.
   256	
   257	### Why this matters
   258	
   259	`APIMethodParameter` validates that the method name passed to `processReturn()` exists in the framework's API method index. This index is built by scanning the test application's source folders (`tests/application/assets/classes/`). Classes in `AppFrameworkTestClasses/` are invisible to this discovery process and will trigger a "method not found" validation error.
   260	
   261	Simple stubs that do not invoke `processReturn()` (e.g., those only used via `createStub()` / `createMock()`) can still reside in `AppFrameworkTestClasses/`.
   262	
   263	---
   264	
   265	## Live-HTTP Tests
   266	
   267	Some tests make real HTTP requests to `APP_URL` (the running test application). These tests are
   268	marked with the `#[Group('live-http')]` PHP attribute (PHPUnit 13) and are **excluded from the
   269	default `composer test` run** via the `<groups><exclude>` block in `phpunit.xml`.
   270	
   271	> **PHPUnit 13 note:** The legacy `@group` docblock annotation is silently ignored by PHPUnit 13.
   272	> Always use the `#[Group(...)]` PHP 8 attribute with a `use PHPUnit\Framework\Attributes\Group;`
   273	> import. Using the annotation form has no effect and will not exclude the test from the default run.
   274	
   275	To run live-HTTP tests, a web server must be available at `APP_URL` (configured in
   276	`tests/application/config/test-ui-config.php` via the `TESTS_BASE_URL` constant). Run them
   277	explicitly with:
   278	
   279	```
   280	composer test-group -- live-http
   281	```
   282	
   283	Tests in this group:
   284	
   285	| Test Class | Methods |
   286	|---|---|
   287	| `AppFrameworkTests\Ajax\AjaxRequestTest` | All (class-level `#[Group('live-http')]`) |
   288	| `AppFrameworkTests\Connectors\RequestTest` | `test_adapterSockets`, `test_adapterCURL` |
   289	
   290	Do not remove the `#[Group('live-http')]` attribute or the `phpunit.xml` exclusion — without it,
   291	the CI pipeline and local runs without a web server will fail with network errors.
   292	
   293	---
   294	
   295	## Superglobal Teardown
   296	
   297	### Automatic $_REQUEST restore
   298	
   299	`ApplicationTestCase` now automatically backs up `$_REQUEST` in `setUp()` and restores it in
   300	`tearDown()`. This prevents inter-test pollution when test files write to `$_REQUEST` without
msg.name: read_file

msg.content:
301	explicit cleanup.
   302	
   303	**No per-class tearDown required for `$_REQUEST`.** Test classes that modify `$_REQUEST` no
   304	longer need to manually unset those keys — the base class restore handles it globally.
   305	
   306	### Other superglobals
   307	
   308	`ApplicationTestCase` does **not** automatically restore `$_GET`, `$_POST`, or `$_SESSION`.
   309	Test classes that write to these superglobals must still unset those keys in their own
   310	`tearDown()` before calling `parent::tearDown()`.
   311	
   312	### Why this matters
   313	
   314	`BaseRecordSelectionTieIn::getRecord()` (and similar request-state-reading classes) caches
   315	the first result it finds. If a previous test left a key in `$_REQUEST`, the next test in the
   316	same file will read a stale cached value, causing assertions that depend on "nothing selected"
   317	to fail — only when the tests are run as a file, not in isolation. This is a classic
   318	inter-test pollution signature that is difficult to diagnose.
   319	
   320	The automatic `$_REQUEST` backup/restore in `ApplicationTestCase` eliminates this category of
   321	bug for the most common superglobal.
   322	
   323	### Convention (for $_GET, $_POST, $_SESSION)
   324	
   325	```php
   326	protected function tearDown() : void
   327	{
   328	    // Unset every $_GET, $_POST, or $_SESSION key written by this test class.
   329	    // (No need to unset $_REQUEST keys — ApplicationTestCase handles those automatically.)
   330	    unset(
   331	        $_GET['some_key'],
   332	        $_POST['some_other_key']
   333	    );
   334	
   335	    parent::tearDown();
   336	}
   337	```
   338	
   339	---
   340	
   341	## PHPUnit Mock Conventions
   342	
   343	PHPUnit 13 emits a **Notice** — "No expectations were configured for the mock object for X"
   344	— when `createMock()` is used without any `expects()` call. Use `createStub()` instead when
   345	the test only needs a double that returns values (no call-count verification):
   346	
   347	```php
   348	// Correct — test only needs the object to return a value; no expectation needed
   349	$method = $this->createStub(APIMethodInterface::class);
   350	
   351	// Avoid — triggers a PHPUnit Notice when no expects() are added
   352	$method = $this->createMock(APIMethodInterface::class);
   353	```
   354	
   355	When writing helper methods that return a test double, annotate the return type with
   356	`&\PHPUnit\Framework\MockObject\Stub` (not `MockObject`) to match `createStub()`'s
   357	actual return type:
   358	
   359	```php
   360	/** @return APIMethodInterface&\PHPUnit\Framework\MockObject\Stub */
   361	private function createMethodStub() : APIMethodInterface
   362	{
   363	    return $this->createStub(APIMethodInterface::class);
   364	}
   365	```
   366	
   367	Use `createMock()` only when the test explicitly verifies interaction (e.g., `expects(once())`).

   184	
   185	API-specific traits in `tests/AppFrameworkTestClasses/API/`:
   186	
   187	| Trait | Interface | Purpose |
   188	|---|---|---|
   189	| `APIClientTestTrait` | `APIClientTestInterface` | API client testing |
   190	| `APIMethodTestTrait` | `APIMethodTestInterface` | API method testing |
   191	
   192	---
   193	
   194	## Bootstrap Process
   195	
   196	The test bootstrap (`tests/bootstrap.php`):
   197	
   198	1. Defines `APP_ROOT` pointing to `tests/application/` (the framework test application).
   199	2. Defines `TESTS_ROOT`, `APP_INSTALL_FOLDER`, `APP_VENDOR_PATH` constants.
   200	3. Sets `APP_FRAMEWORK_TESTS = true` to signal the framework's own test suite.
   201	4. Requires the framework bootstrap (`src/classes/Application/Bootstrap/Bootstrap.php`).
   202	5. Initializes `Application_Bootstrap` and boots the `TestSuiteBootstrap` class.
   203	
   204	This means the full application stack is available in tests (database, services, configuration).
   205	
   206	### Transaction Shutdown Handler
   207	
   208	During `_boot()`, `TestSuiteBootstrap` calls `registerTransactionCleanupHandler()`, which registers a PHP shutdown function that invokes `DBHelper::rollbackConditional()`. This handler fires whenever the PHP process exits — including after a crash, fatal error, or `Ctrl-C` during a test run.
   209	
   210	**Why this matters:** If a test process dies mid-transaction (e.g., due to an out-of-memory error or an unhandled signal), InnoDB keeps the row locks held by that transaction until it times out. Subsequent test runs that try to acquire the same locks stall for the full `innodb_lock_wait_timeout` duration (default: 50 seconds). The shutdown handler ensures those locks are released immediately by rolling back any open transaction when the process terminates.
   211	
   212	`DBHelper::rollbackConditional()` is guarded by `isTransactionStarted()` — it is a no-op when no transaction is active, so there is no risk of interfering with a test run that completed normally.
   213	
   214	---
   215	
   216	## Framework Test Application
   217	
   218	The framework includes a working test application in `tests/application/` that provides concrete implementations of framework abstractions. This application is used by the test suite to exercise framework features against real database tables and screens.
   219	
   220	---
   221	
   222	## Local Test Environment Setup
   223	
   224	The test suite requires local configuration files that are **not committed** to the repository. Before running tests for the first time, copy the distribution templates and configure them for the local environment:
   225	
   226	1. Copy `tests/application/config/test-db-config.dist.php` → `tests/application/config/test-db-config.php`
   227	2. Copy `tests/application/config/test-ui-config.dist.php` → `tests/application/config/test-ui-config.php`
   228	3. Copy `tests/application/config/test-cas-config.dist.php` → `tests/application/config/test-cas-config.php`
   229	
   230	Edit `test-db-config.php` and set the correct database host, name, user, and password. The database name defaults to `app_framework_testsuite`; import `tests/sql/testsuite.sql` to initialise it.
   231	
   232	Edit `test-ui-config.php` and adjust `TESTS_BASE_URL` to the URL at which `tests/application` is reachable on the local webserver.
   233	
   234	`test-cas-config.php` is only required when `TESTS_SESSION_TYPE` is set to `CAS` in `test-ui-config.php`. For most local runs the default `NoAuth` session type is sufficient and the CAS config can be left as-is.
   235	
   236	### Seeding the Test Database
   237	
   238	After importing `tests/sql/testsuite.sql`, the test database must also be seeded with system users before running the test suite:
   239	
   240	```
   241	composer seed-tests
   242	```
   243	
   244	This command runs `tests/seed-test-db.php`, which calls `TestSuiteBootstrap::seedSystemUsers()`. The method starts a transaction, executes the `InitSystemUsers` installer task to insert the required system user records, and commits on success (rolling back on any failure).
   245	
   246	**If system users are missing when the test suite boots**, `TestSuiteBootstrap::configureUsers()` throws a `BootException` (error code `175001`) with a message listing the missing user IDs and directing the developer to run `composer seed-tests`. You will see an error similar to:
   247	
   248	```
   249	BootException: System users [2, 5] are missing from the test database. Run: composer seed-tests
   250	```
   251	
   252	Re-run `composer seed-tests` to resolve it. Seeding is a one-time operation per database instance; it only needs to be repeated if the database is dropped and re-imported.
   253	
   254	---
